previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with worsening dyspnea and hypoxia two days after completing a course of moxifloxacin and a prednisone taper for a recent pneumonia. Despite treatment, his shortness of breath, cough, and sputum production had worsened. Imaging showed no new pneumonia but findings consistent with COPD exacerbation and possible Velcade-induced pneumonitis. He responded well to a high-dose steroid taper and a short course of antibiotics. A CT without contrast showed improvement in prior lung changes. An abdominal ultrasound revealed interval enlargement of his abdominal aortic aneurysm to 5.2 cm, prompting a vascular surgery follow-up. Warfarin was restarted, and Bactrim was resumed for Pneumocystis prophylaxis due to immunosuppression. He improved clinically, was weaned off supplemental oxygen, and discharged home with a steroid taper, antibiotics, and close follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M w/a history of multiple myeloma, COPD, and h/o recurrent 
pneumonia (requiring intubation) who p/w SOB, fever and CXR 
demonstrating new left lower pneumonia.
.
# Left lower PNA:  Pt initially presented with fevers, cough, 
and dyspnea. On admission he appeared fatigued. He was having 
shortness of breath more than his baseline. He was also 
producing brown sputum. He had scattered wheezes throughout and 
rhonchi in his left lower lobe. Blood cultures and sputum 
cultures were sent. Sputum gram stain showed 1+ gram positive 
rods and 1+ gram negative rods, sparse commensal respiratory 
flora on culture, with negative PCP, ___ AFB smear and 
fungal. Aspergillus galactomanan was sent and was pending on 
discharge. He was started on Cefepime, Vancomycin, and 
Levofloxacin. During his admission his cough improved and his 
sputum changed from brown to white. On the day of discharge he 
was only having minimal shortness of breath with exertion, at 
his baseline. He remained afebrile. He completed 4 days of 
Levofloxacin, Cefepime and Vancomycin and was switched to po 
Levofloxacin on the day of discharge to complete 14 day course.
.
# COPD: He had scattered wheezes on admission and increased 
shortness of breath. He was started on med nebs and continued on 
Spiriva and Advair. He required no supplemental oxygen. His O2 
sats remained >92% on room air. His SOB had improved to baseline 
on discharge. He was instructed to continue his Symbicort and 
Spiriva at home.
He was scheduled to follow-up with Dr. ___ on ___.
